Both the reference and a separate explicit launch directive appear in the same message. Recorded this way so the audit trail states what actually happened rather than a tidier version.

Falsifier: programs at retained_fraction ~1.000 with median ~16 primitives mean the repair did not help regardless of bind rate; measured success shape is median 31 primitives at retained 0.630, band 0.52-0.96.

reseal_supersession.method: Applied as four individual visible file edits rather than a script, after an automated rewrite was correctly refused as self-modification. The original authorization record above is left UNEDITED as the historical record of what was first approved.
reseal_supersession.root_cause: The base contract pinned src/compose_v4/experiments/pmo_population_live_parent_gate.py at 518045a7, its PRE-EDIT hash. That file was re-pointed from the beam binder to the realizer AFTER the integration resealed, so on disk it is 2b44294b. Exactly one pin mismatched; the runtime identity guard caught it inside the container before any oracle call was charged.
reseal_supersession.why_this_is_not_a_scope_change: The authorization sentence the owner approved already describes this runtime -- it authorizes the run 'on the basis that the re-pointed live-parent support gate PASSES under the realizer the controller actually binds through'. The re-pointed gate file is precisely what is now correctly pinned. Nothing about tasks, budgets, comparators or the predeclared read changed; only the pin that had not caught up.
